title: Practice worksheet
description: A self-marking practice worksheet. One file is one worksheet, rendered by <practice-worksheet> and graded by /js/practice.js. Answers ship in the served markup, so a worksheet may only ever be built from material whose answers are already published to students — a practice paper that prints its own key, never a live test.

$schema.description: Relative path to this schema, so the editor validates and documents fields inline.

title.description: The page title, used in the browser tab and navigation. Not shown in the body.

description.description: One sentence for the page's meta description.

indexed.description: Set false to keep the page out of the sitemap and search results. Does NOT gate publishing — the page is still served to anyone with the URL.

eyebrow.description: Small-caps label above the heading, after the term and course code.

lede.description: One line under the heading: what this is for, and whether it is graded.

intro.description: Introductory paragraphs: how to use the worksheet, and what it covers.

terms.description: The vocabulary bank. Each term renders as a button whose definition opens in a popover anchored to it.

sections.description: The worksheet's sections, in the order students meet them. Mirror the real paper's sections and order so practice transfers.

footer.description: Closing paragraphs: where to go back to when something did not land. Omit for no footer.

links.description: Links listed under the footer paragraphs, resolved the same way a citation is.

checkMode.description: How a student checks answers. "end" (the default, or the site's `worksheets.checkMode`): only See results at the end. "question": also a Check answer button on each gradable question.

copy.description: Overrides for the components' own wording — button labels, the privacy notice, the "Answer:" prefix. Every key has a course-neutral default in prepareWorksheet; set only what this worksheet says differently.

source.description: Where an answer comes from. Name a slide by week/day/slide and the URL is built for you; use href for anything else. Cite only what a student can see — a fact that lives in a ::: notes block is not a citation they can follow.

label.description: How the citation reads, e.g. "Week 3 · Tuesday — Naming the regions: landmarks".

day.description: Deck day number, 1 for the week's first meeting.

slide.description: Slide number within the deck; becomes the #sN anchor.

href.description: An explicit URL, for a reading or guide rather than a slide. Wins over week/day/slide. A site path ("/local-setup-guide/") is made absolute against site.hostname, because a worksheet is a single file students download; an external URL is used as written.

quote.description: The line from that source that settles the answer. Shown under the link.

term.description: The term as students will look for it.

definition.description: One or two sentences, in the course's own words.

legendEntry.description: One verdict a judge question may be given. Order is the order of the radio buttons.

letter.description: The letter students write on paper.
The letter students write in the box.

blank.description: One box a student fills in.

label.description: What the box is asking for. Self-numbering, as the list is unnumbered.

accept.description: Every wording that counts as right. Both sides are normalized before comparison — case, angle brackets, slashes and separators are ignored — so list only genuinely different answers, not punctuation variants.

display.description: The answer as it is shown when the student got it wrong.

n.description: Section number, matching the real paper.

blurb.description: One line on what the section tests.

legend.description: Required by `judge` questions: the verdicts on offer, shared by every snippet in the section.

question.description: One item. `kind` decides which other fields apply; every kind takes id, prompt, why and sources.

id.description: Section and number, e.g. "3.4". Shown to the student and used to build every input name on the question, so it must be unique across the worksheet.

kind.description: choice: one right option. match: items against a lettered bank. fill: text blanks with an optional word bank. tree: a DOM tree with blanks to name. grid: a row/column table of judgements. judge: a code snippet given a verdict plus the offending line. selfcheck: marked by the student against a revealed answer.

code.description: A snippet shown above the controls. Rendered verbatim, so say "below" in the prompt, not "above".

lang.description: The snippet fence's language, e.g. python. Picks the Prism grammar the snippet is highlighted with; an unknown or missing one renders plain.

figure.description: An inline SVG diagram, written in the authored file as an ```svg fence. Styled by 's class vocabulary — region, dashed, label, small, pin — never by hex values, so it follows the theme. Never a raster: an is a broken image in an uploaded copy of the page.

dragDrop.description: match and fill only: make the bank draggable onto the answers. A pointer affordance layered over the select or input, never a replacement — the control stays the keyboard, touch and screen-reader path.

dragHint.description: The line telling students they may drag or use the control. Say both.

why.description: The reasoning, revealed once the question is checked. Explain why the right answer is right, not just what it is.

sources.description: Where the answer is taught. Rendered as the "?" beside the question.

options.description: choice: the options, in display order.

answer.description: choice: the index into options. judge: the index into the section's legend.

bank.description: match: the lettered options. fill: the word bank, as plain strings.

items.description: match: the things to be matched, each with the bank letter that answers it.

blanks.description: fill and tree: the boxes to fill.

nodes.description: tree: the tree, in reading order. A node is either a given label or a blank referring to blanks[] by index.

label.description: A node already filled in. Omit for a blank.

blank.description: Index into blanks[]. Omit for a filled node.

rowHeader.description: grid: the heading over the rows, e.g. Behavior. The table's first header cell.

columns.description: grid: the column headings, e.g. Works / Doesn't work.

lines.description: judge: the snippet, one array entry per line. Each becomes a selectable line.

lineAnswers.description: judge: indexes of the lines that cause the problem. An empty array means the snippet is fine, and "no line" becomes the right pick.

reveal.description: selfcheck: the model answer, shown when the student asks for it.

checkYourself.description: selfcheck: the specific things to compare against, as a checklist. Marking by eye needs criteria, not just the answer.
